facts.text: Indiana 13, Michigan 6, in overtime, at Michigan Stadium. Michigan falls to 4-3 overall, 1-3 in the Big Ten.
Michigan has not scored a touchdown in more than 60 minutes of game time. The only touchdown of the game was Indiana QB Hoover's 4-yard run on the second snap of overtime.
Michigan's tying field goal went through with two seconds left in regulation.
Indiana's first 3 points: Carr's late pitch on a speed option was fumbled, Indiana ball at the Michigan 28. Seven plays, 24 yards, a 22-yard field goal.
Indiana's second 3 points: Carr's pass meant for Buchanan in triple coverage was tipped and intercepted. A 34-yard field goal followed.
Indiana's overtime touchdown: from the 25, Hoover to Schott for 21, then Hoover ran it in from 4. Two plays.
Indiana never scored on a drive that started in its own territory.
Michigan's defense allowed 212 total yards to the defending national champions, and 127 rushing yards through four quarters, with no touchdown in regulation.
Indiana QB Hoover was 8-of-18 for 81 yards in regulation and threw his first interception of the season. Zeke Berry returned it 37 yards to the Indiana 13.
Chris Bracy had 13 tackles. Smith Snowden had a sack to open the fourth quarter.
Last week's Michigan Weekly Card 12 said Hoover had zero interceptions and six different Michigan players had one.
Michigan's offense: 224 total yards; 42 carries for 57 yards, 1.4 a carry.
Carr, in his first start: 20-of-32 for 167 yards, an interception and a lost fumble.

The second half opened with a 61-yard, eight-minute drive to third-and-goal at the 1. Offensive coordinator Jason Beck called play-action; Osunsanmi sacked Carr for minus-13, and the short field goal that followed missed.
After Berry's interception set Michigan up at the Indiana 13, Michigan ran four plays for two yards and kicked a field goal.
On3: in overtime Michigan got one first down, then Moa dropped a pass on 4th-and-5.
Another writeup: the overtime fourth down was 4th-and-9, incomplete to Moa.
Michigan has scored under 20 points in 5 of 7 games, and averages 15.4 points a game against Power Four teams. It has scored more than 21 only once all year, against UTEP.

Kicker Butkowski missed a 53-yarder before halftime and the short kick after the goal-line sack; he made field goals of 29 and 26, including the tying kick. He had missed once all year before Saturday.
Michigan has two muffed punts this season (the opener and Minnesota). Minnesota turned mishandled punts and coverage into three points. Against Iowa, in a one-point loss, kickoff coverage broke down.
Kyle Whittingham on the goal-line call, quoted: "That was not a good football call."
Whittingham, quoted: "Everything falls on my shoulders. So whatever happens in the course of a game is on me."
Whittingham on Beck, quoted: "I'm not going to say he's struggling."
Whittingham, quoted: "If that's the number 6 team in the country, then we're a pretty good football team, even though we're sitting here at 4-3."
Whittingham on Sunday, quoted: "We've got to be better than that on offense. There's no way around it."

Michigan Weekly's own record this season: in August the show budgeted two losses (at Oregon, at Ohio State); Michigan has three losses, none of them budgeted. Episode 2 said 'better team, worse record'. Episode 2 said the models were grading a special-teams unit Michigan replaced. Week 2 coined 'the Leipold floor: run it, raise the floor'; Michigan ran for 174 yards in the second half against Penn State. Indiana week the show said 4.5 yards a carry between the tackles. Indiana week the show took Michigan +7.5.
Most books closed at Indiana -7.5, so Michigan covered by a half point. If a book had -7 it was a push.
CBS had Penn State -6.5 as the closing line for Michigan's Penn State game.

Firing Whittingham would cost about $23-25 million by the show's estimate (75% of the remaining base on his $41 million deal). If he leaves before Feb. 1, 2027, he owes Michigan $5 million, and he keeps his signing bonus only if he stays past Jan. 31.
December signing day, the early-January transfer portal window and NIL money all fall in the same winter calendar.
Michigan's 2027 recruiting class was ranked 12th nationally last week. Michigan flipped a 2027 receiver from Toledo last week.
Michigan's defense, under Whittingham hire Jay Hill, ranks fourth in the country.

Rutgers is 2-5, 1-3 in the Big Ten; 1-5 against FBS teams. Results: L 21-37 UMass (home), L 21-28 at Boston College, L 35-42 USC, W 58-7 Howard, L 15-47 Indiana, W 37-30 at Maryland, L 14-42 at No. 24 Northwestern.

Greg Schiano is 32-44 since returning to Rutgers in 2020, went 5-7 last year, and opened this season losing 37-21 at home to UMass as a 29.5-point favorite. Firing him after this season would cost about $18.5 million.
Rutgers starting QB Dylan Lonergan was hurt on the third play at Northwestern. The two backups went 9-of-27 for 100 yards with two interceptions. No injury detail yet.
Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond had 150 yards on 18 carries at Northwestern. Receiver KJ Duff had 196 yards and three touchdowns in the opener.

Rutgers allows 37.6 points a game against FBS teams and at least 28 in every FBS game. Northwestern ran for 285 yards and went 9-of-13 on third down against Rutgers. Indiana put up 593 yards on Rutgers.
Kickoff time and TV for Michigan at Rutgers were not confirmed when the facts were gathered.

Michigan's remaining games: at Rutgers, Michigan State, at Oregon, UCLA, at Ohio State. Bowl eligibility needs two wins in the last five; eight wins needs four of five. Michigan hasn't missed eight wins in a full season since 2014.
Michigan is 9-1 all-time against Rutgers. The only loss was the first meeting, 26-24 in Piscataway in 2014. The last meeting was 31-7 in Ann Arbor in 2023. No meetings in 2024 or 2025.
Between Schiano and Whittingham, more than $40 million in buyouts will be on the same field.
Suggested one-number picks: 200 rushing yards (Northwestern ran for 285), or a Michigan touchdown before halftime.
Nick's own Indiana-week picks, to read back on air, included a first-drive personnel call: 11 personnel or Rhino (from his rewatch).
The betting line and total for Michigan at Rutgers were not available when the facts were gathered.
